_doc: provenance.py sentinel table (Seed B): the NAMED false negatives of a system of record, as data. A reading that trips one reads as UNKNOWN, never as 'none' / 'zero' / 'not scheduled'. A rule trips when every condition under `when` holds: kind (one of), source_re (regex over the source string), field (one of), value_in (one of; null, 0, '', false), context (each key equals the reading's context value; a list = one of). `why` is the plain-words reason the gate repeats. These are the engine's generic shapes; an organization's own table names its system of record's reports and fields (the production pack keeps that file beside its binding).

sentinels.name: filtered_report_count_zero
sentinels.why: a filtered pull of the system of record can come back empty for a record that exists; zero rows from a filtered pull is unknown, never none

sentinels.name: report_null_schedule_timestamp
sentinels.why: a report row can carry a null schedule timestamp while the job is scheduled; the schedule is unknown until the record itself is opened

sentinels.name: windowed_report_absent
sentinels.why: a date-windowed pull does not show records outside its window; absence from it is unknown, never gone

sentinels.name: cached_count_null
sentinels.why: a null count in a cache means not checked, never zero
